sources.entry: sortedcontainers - Fast and pure-Python implementation of sorted collections.

summary.one_liner: A pure-Python library providing fast sorted collections (SortedList, SortedDict, SortedSet) that need no C compiler or extensions.
summary.what_it_does: Provides three sorted container types: SortedList, SortedDict, and SortedSet. The README shows examples of creating them from unsorted input, indexing and slicing, counting values, popping items from a sorted dict by index, and using bisect_left on a sorted set. It states that the operations run in faster than linear time. The containers split data into smaller fragments to avoid O(N) insertion costs. The README says the API is nearly identical to the older blist and bintrees modules. It also describes help() access to docs and a user guide with performance comparisons.
use_cases: keep a sorted list of values that changes often
maintain a dictionary ordered by its keys
store unique items in sorted order
find the largest or smallest keys in a dict
replace a red-black or AVL tree with a simpler structure
sorted index lookups with bisect in Python
notable: Pure-Python with no C extensions, so no compiler is needed to install
SortedSet is a Python set with a SortedList index
Splits data into fragments to avoid O(N) insertion costs
API nearly identical to the older blist and bintrees modules
Fully documented with benchmark comparisons against alternatives
caveats: The README's demo notes that the sample multiplying a sorted list by ten million takes nearly a gigabyte of memory
Stores a reference (8 bytes) per element, so memory use grows with size
